summary:
We developed an interactive web-based platform called Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map to make Mars exploration more accessible and understandable. The project combines an interactive Mars map with scientific information and exploration-related features.
Users can zoom, pan, and select locations on the Martian surface to explore geographical information and understand the challenges of the Martian environment. By bringing different exploration features and NASA-related data together in one platform, our project makes complex planetary information easier to visualize and understand.
This project addresses the challenge of making Mars exploration information more accessible through interactive technology. Its goal is to encourage scientific curiosity, support space education, and demonstrate how planetary data can contribute to understanding future Mars exploration and mission-planning concepts.
details:
Project Details: Interplanetary Survival Guide – Martian Map

1. What does your project do and how does it work?

Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map is an interactive web-based platform designed to help users explore Mars and understand the challenges of planetary exploration. It brings together an interactive Martian map and NASA-related scientific information in one application.

Users can interact with the Mars map by zooming, panning, and selecting different locations. The platform presents relevant geographical and scientific information to help users understand the Martian environment. Different modules work together to provide a unified exploration experience, making complex planetary information easier to access and understand.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Makes Mars exploration more interactive and accessible.
  • Helps users understand Martian geography and environmental conditions.
  • Brings different types of NASA-related information into one platform.
  • Encourages scientific curiosity and space exploration.
  • Provides an educational experience for students, researchers, and space enthusiasts.
  • Demonstrates how scientific data can be transformed into useful visual information.

3. What is the intended impact?

Our intended impact is to make planetary exploration more understandable and accessible to everyone. The project aims to encourage interest in space science, improve awareness of the challenges of exploring Mars, and demonstrate the value of using scientific data for exploration and mission-planning concepts.

In the long term, this concept could be expanded with additional NASA datasets, improved terrain information, and more advanced exploration features to support future Mars research and educational activities.

4. What tools did you use?

Our team used a combination of web development tools, programming technologies, and space-related data resources.

  • HTML: To structure the website and its modules.
  • CSS: To design the interface and create an engaging user experience.
  • JavaScript: To implement interactive features and functionality.
  • NASA data resources: To incorporate scientific information about Mars.
  • GitHub: For collaborative development, code sharing, version control, and integrating our team members' contributions.
  • Antigravity IDE: To assist with development, coding, and project integration.
  • Google Chrome: To run and test the web application.

5. How is your project creative?

The creativity of our project comes from combining multiple aspects of Mars exploration into a single interactive platform instead of presenting scientific information as static text or separate resources.

Our approach connects geographical exploration with scientific information, allowing users to interact with Mars and discover information through a visual experience. The modular structure also allows different features to work together as parts of one larger exploration guide.

By making space-related information interactive and user-friendly, we aim to turn complex scientific concepts into an engaging digital experience.

6. What factors did your team consider?

During development, our team considered several important factors:

  • Scientific relevance: Using NASA-related information to maintain the educational and scientific value of the project.
  • User experience: Creating a simple, understandable, and interactive interface.
  • Accessibility: Making the platform easy to explore without requiring advanced scientific knowledge.
  • Accuracy: Considering the importance of reliable planetary information and avoiding misleading representations.
  • Integration: Developing separate modules that can function together as one unified website.
  • Scalability: Designing the project so that additional features and scientific datasets can be incorporated in the future.
  • Educational value: Ensuring that the platform encourages learning, curiosity, and interest in planetary science.

Overall Goal

Our goal is to transform the way people explore and understand Mars by combining interactive technology, scientific information, and creative web development into one unified Interplanetary Survival Guide.
